content: Nicotinamide, also referred to as niacinamide, is the amide form of niacin (vitamin B3) and has the chemical formula C6H6N2O. It is frequently utilized as an ingredient in energy drinks. Nicotinamide is a water-soluble component of the vitamin B complex group. Within the body, nicotinamide is integrated into nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD) and nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate (NADP). These molecules serve as coenzymes in numerous enzymatic oxidation-reduction reactions that are critical for processes such as tissue respiration, lipid metabolism, and glycogenolysis. Nicotinamide has demonstrated anti-inflammatory properties, which may be advantageous for patients suffering from inflammatory acne vulgaris. These effects include, but are not limited to, the suppression of antigen-induced lymphocytic transformation and the inhibition of 3'-5' cyclic AMP phosphodiesterase. Additionally, nicotinamide has shown the ability to counteract the inflammatory effects of iodides, which are known to trigger or worsen inflammatory acne. Unlike nicotinic acid (niacin), nicotinamide does not exhibit vasodilatory, gastrointestinal, hepatic, or hypolipidemic effects. Consequently, nicotinamide does not cause the flushing, itching, or burning sensations of the skin that are commonly associated with the oral administration of high doses of nicotinic acid or niacin.
